resources.string: Your Dom keeps Google Authenticator, or a compatible app, on their own phone. It generates short-lived codes they can share with you from anywhere.
Remove this authenticator? Your Dom’s codes will stop opening Dom controls. Your Dom PIN will still work.
On your Dom’s phone: Google Authenticator → + → Scan a QR code.
Enter the displayed key manually in your authenticator.
Keys handed over. Your Dom’s next fresh code can open Dom controls.
Code expired, already used, or incorrect. Check automatic time on both phones and try a fresh code.
Too many attempts. Wait before trying another code, or use the Dom PIN.
Authenticator unavailable. Use the Dom PIN to pair it again.
Use an ordered range between 0.5 and 720 hours.
A Pact is already active, or the new Pact could not be saved.
Your Dom has the setup key in Google Authenticator or their chosen authenticator. Ask for the current six-digit code when you need Dom access.
Your Dom adds the QR code or manual setup key to Google Authenticator (or a compatible app). They do not need SubHub.
Their authenticator generates a new six-digit code every 30 seconds. Ask them to share the current code when they approve access.
Choose Keyholder code at a Dom prompt and enter the code before it expires. It opens the same controls as the PIN.
No timed Pact is active. Choose your lock on Home, then enter service when you are ready.
Choose the way that fits your arrangement. PIN and authenticator both open the same Dom controls; codes do not send remote commands.
Ask your Dom for the code showing in their authenticator.
Nothing changes until you confirm. Keep the pairing key private.
